title: Shipping the OpenCode context hook in the profile makes every OpenCode first start install the plugin SDK, and fails it with no network
foundBy: sandbox CI on 7ea098e: every OpenCode agent-replay job failed on its first turn, on podman, Firecracker and macOS alike

evidence.verified: Unit: `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestOpenCodeProfileShipsNoPlugin|TestOpenCodeWrapperLinksTheHookOnlyWithALine|TestOpenCodeTurnWaitsForTheFirstSessionWithALine' -count=1` PASS; the wrapper test fails with the link made unconditionally, and the driver test fails with the single ask restored. Replay: `make test-agents-replay AGENTS_REPLAY_CASES='TestAgentReplay/opencode-.*-shared$'` on the slim CI image built from this tree: 3 of 3 cells PASS, `cs-vcr served 6 request(s) and missed 0`; on 7ea098e the same cells failed on their first turn. Live: a campaign of three OpenCode members, every one with a line, on the full image built from this tree. Each member's first start logged `the server answers but gave no session yet; waiting for its first start to finish` and then finished with exit 0; no member was continued. The campaign met its mission in 24 minutes 36 seconds with 4 hand-offs. The orchestrator handed off at 40,688 tokens over a line of 40,000, and the agents once and twice on their dispatch. The run before this fix, on the same profile, continued every member once at readback. `make check` passed every gate on this commit, with the partial smoke tier the replay leaves set aside.

resolution: The hook ships at `~/.local/share/cs-opencode/plugins/cs-context-hook.ts`, outside the profile. `cs-opencode` links it into `~/.cs-opencode/plugins/` only when `CS_HANDOFF_TOKENS` names a line, and says so on stderr when the hook is missing rather than failing the start. A member with no line starts as it did before the hook. With a line, `cs-opencode-turn` asks for the first session up to twelve times, ten seconds each, while OpenCode's one-time SDK install runs, and once as before without a line.
details:
The context hook for OpenCode is a plugin, and 143ac79 shipped it in the profile's plugins directory, `~/.cs-opencode/plugins/`, for every member. OpenCode installs its plugin SDK, `@opencode-ai/plugin`, from npm on every start, into each config directory it reads. When a config directory holds a plugin, it holds the first session until that install is done. In a CI replay the network is a recorder that answers no npm request, so the install hung. The turn driver asks for a session once, for ten seconds, and the ask came back empty: `cs-opencode-turn: could not create an opencode session (got '')`, exit 3. That was 15 of 15 OpenCode cells. The same first-start failure had been seen on every OpenCode member of two live campaigns and taken for a flake. With the network the install finishes within a minute, and the next turn found the session.

Reproduced in a sandbox from the same image with `HTTP_PROXY` pointed at a closed port, as the replay sets it: the first turn fails at 11 seconds. The same turn on a machine whose profile already holds the SDK succeeds. A fresh machine with the SDK copied into the profile alone still fails, because OpenCode runs the install for its other config directory too.

A member with no hand-off line has no use for the plugin and must start exactly as before this feature. A member with a line needs the install once per machine, with the network, and its first start has to be given the time.

notes.text: Baking the SDK into the image was tried and set aside: OpenCode installs it per config directory, and making that reliable would depend on its installer's internals. It stays an option if the one-time install on a lined machine proves slow.
